verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 mission returned to Earth on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Splashdown is targeted for 8:07 p.m. EDT ... on April 1 [launch, implying return ~10 days later]'; R2: 'Updated April 10, 2026 ... The voyage concludes Friday, April 10'; R3: 'SPLASHDOWN! ... at 8:07 p.m. EDT'; R5: 'return to Earth tonight, April 10'; R6: 'splashed down ... at 8:07 p.m. ET'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm splashdown/return on April 10, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 mission had a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego'; R3: 'splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego'; R5: 'splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California'; R6: 'splash down off the coast of San Diego'
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources explicitly state the splashdown location as Pacific Ocean off San Diego.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 mission had a four-person crew.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: lists 'Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch and ... Jeremy Hansen'; R2: 'four astronauts'; R3: lists four; R4: 'four-person crew'; R5: 'four astronauts'; R6: lists four
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm exactly four crew members by name or count.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 mission crew completed a 10-day mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'historic 10-day journey'; R3: 'approximate 10-day mission'; R4: '10-day mission'; R5: '10-day trip to the moon'; R6: '10-day journey ... 10-day mission'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly describe the mission as 10 days.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 mission crew orbited the moon.
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: R1: 'historic lunar flyby' (not orbit); R2: 'circling the moon'; R4: 'orbiting the moon'; R5: 'trip to the moon and back'; R6: 'journey around the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Sources conflict: R1 specifies 'flyby' (no orbit), while R4 says 'orbiting' and others use 'circling/around' which could imply orbit.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 mission crew traveled further from Earth than any human in history.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'traveling further than any human in history'; R6: 'farther from Earth than anyone in human history'
verifications.reasoning: Directly supported by R2 and R6; no contradictions.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 mission splashdown occurred at 8:07 p.m. EDT on Friday, April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Splashdown is targeted for 8:07 p.m. EDT'; R3: 'SPLASHDOWN! ... at 8:07 p.m. EDT'; R5: '8:07 p.m. EDT ... April 10'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm exact time in EDT on April 10; R6 uses ET which aligns.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 mission splashdown occurred at 5:07 p.m. PDT on Friday, April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly provide the PDT equivalent for the same event on April 10.
